newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Vanguard in many cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Vanguard in many cooperation talks.

text.p: Vanguard Medica Plc, which earlier reported deeper losses as it speeded up clinical trial programmes, said it expected to sign a co-operation agreement with another biotech or pharmaceutical firm later this year.

Chief executive Robert Mansfield told Reuters Vanguard was in talks with a host of companies to jointly develop or sell drugs after it already struck a deal with SmithKline Beecham, which will market anti-migraine drug VML 251.

"The succes we've had with SmithKline Beecham has been interesting for other pharmaceutical companies and we're talking to quite a few very significant pharma companies around the world about doing similar collaborations," Mansfield said.
"Our ability to develop things rapidly is also very attractive to biotech companies in Europe and the U.S. So we are getting a lot of approaches from those companies too," he added.
Vanguard said earlier that clinical programmes for its drugs against migraine, hyperphosphataemia and inflammatory diseases were ahead of schedule.
This resulted in a 1996 pre-tax loss of 10.95 million stg compared with 3.67 million in 1995. Mansfield said the loss was as expected by analysts.
Vanguard's cash position at the end of 1996 was 51.8 million stg, leaving it with enough money for investments this year and 1998.
A new cash raising exercise may take place in about one and a half years from now, Mansfield said after Vanguard last tapped the capital market at its flotation in May.
"Sometime in the next 18 months I expect to be back to talk to the institutions," Mansfield said.
